acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Bears family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Hookclaw, T3, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Grapple Specialist archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two water construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Asymmetric bear with one enlarged hook claw, thickened wrist, lower pulling stance, and matching shoulder overdevelopment.
Signature mechanic: Hook and Haul: one enlarged curved claw catches the target while the opposite hind foot becomes a visible towing anchor.
battlefieldDuty: Hook a limb, shield, or obstacle and drag it sideways to break defensive formations.
constructionDimensions: Heavy saturated fur hangs in coherent locks over a solid body while runoff exposes scars and joint direction.
Swipes and roars drive readable sheets or pressure rings, and displaced water emphasizes the bear's mass.
counterplay: Dodge toward the planted foot or strike the exposed inner wrist before the sideways drag begins. Affinity signal: A loaded water layer drains from the inner wrist, hind leg, or chest during recovery, exposing the physical weak point.
forbiddenTreatments: Spray that obscures the body, claws, or terrain lane
identityInvariants: Every form retains a four-legged ursine body, plantigrade paws, compact tail, broad muzzle, dense coat, and weight-bearing shoulder hump.
Escalation uses coat condition, scars, claw specialization, posture, and environmental interaction rather than humanoid equipment.
Raised shoulders, planted hind legs, open chest, and exposed inner wrists preserve readable commitment and recovery windows.
telegraph: The hooked forepaw turns palm-up and the opposite hind foot digs deeply into the ground.
